grammar_errors.mistake: He described خطيبتي (feminine) with masculine عيان; Amal recast عيانة and he repeated 'عيانة' at 02:26.
Amal recast the order to topic + body part + verb (هي راسها بيوجع) and he repeated it at 04:07.
With قلقانين he used لـ for 'about'; Amal said 'You're worried from... Men' and he said من نار - قلقان takes من.
grammar_errors.said: الـ or لا الـ نار. / لـ النار for fire
grammar_errors.fix: Men not. You're worried from. ... Men، men.

grammar_errors.mistake: دير بال takes على; he put خطيبتي straight after بال and Amal recast بالي على خطيبتي. A separate moment from A6 (11:35): two minutes and a full explanation lie between, and she fixed it again there.
Amal named the fixed preposition: بدير بالي takes على; he then said ديرت بالي على خطيبتي.
For the 'take care' command he said ديري باليك; Amal gave the command دير بالك (no -ي on بال).
grammar_errors.fix: دير بالك is actually the command form.

grammar_errors.mistake: After خلينا the verb is a bare present; he used past عملنا and Amal recast نعمل, which he repeated.
Asked what is in the sky he said غيم; Amal asked 'just one?' and he changed to the plural غيوم.
The known sky needs el- (السما); Amal recast السما بالليل and he repeated it.
After the feminine نجمة, تاني must be تانية; Amal echoed تاني as a prompt and he changed to تانية, which she accepted.
With the object fronted the verb needs a pointer; Amal named it and he fixed to بشوفها ('I forgot the pointer rule').

For 'different than' he used من (thinking comparative); Amal gave عن and confirmed it at 32:21, and he ended with الهواء هون غير عن الهواء هناك. Engine wrote بعيد / بيد for غير: Amal never rejected the word and praised بعيد عن الهوا هناك with ممتاز.
grammar_errors.said: آآ، بعيد من cuz it's comparative, right?

grammar_errors.mistake: آخر + el- means 'the end of'; for 'the last time' it is آخر مرة, which Amal explained and he took.
grammar_errors.fix: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time. ... صح. آخر مرة. The last time.

grammar_errors.mistake: The subject مرة is feminine; Amal prompted 'مرة is' and he fixed to كانت.
'I cleaned it' needs the object ending; Amal prompted 'It.' and he said نظفتها.

Asked what things are on the land he gave singular الوردة; Amal's prompt (engine وحدات؟, likely وردات؟) offered a plural, he said وردات and she said Mm. Low: his collective الورد (fine) is stamped at the same second as her prompt, so it may be a self-fix, and her word is uncertain.
He meant the old streets in general (plural); Amal recast الشوارع and he repeated it.
'Made of stone' with مع (with) is wrong; Amal recast the sentence with just حجر ('الشوارع الإدام في أمريكا حجر').
grammar_errors.fix: Or just حجر. Are stone. Made of is different than made.

grammar_errors.mistake: 'The second stone' is تاني حجر or الحجر التاني; حجر تاني is 'another stone'. Amal recast and noted he said it right first.
grammar_errors.fix: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.

grammar_errors.mistake: مفضل is an adjective: it takes el- and never a pronoun ending (Amal 54:46 'المفضل is an adjective', 54:56 'Never takes pronoun ending'); standalone 'my favorite' is المفضل عندي.
grammar_errors.fix: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي. ... Never takes pronoun ending.

grammar_errors.mistake: The adjective goes after the noun; Amal named it ('المفضل is an adjective') and gave الحجر المفضل.
grammar_errors.said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
grammar_errors.fix: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.

grammar_errors.mistake: A noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; Amal said 'No ال first' and he said حجري المفضل.
The adjective after الدرس needs el-; Amal said 'al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders' and gave هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.
grammar_errors.fix: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders. ... هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.
